chapter: Safe streets, decline and club life at San Jacinto
title: Why San Jacinto declined, and cheap prices then
summary: The club declined after the money was mismanaged and members died; prices in the 1930s were very low.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Why did the San Jacinto Hall decline? Did the members just lose interest or their children didn't want to keep on?

Well, on the last part of it, that's what I'm saying now, after that fellow had took the money, started messing with the money and it, you know, and it just went down and all the members, a whole lot of them died. This was more than that? Yeah.
Yeah. And a lot, a lot of the members died, you know, and some of them, something like that. And nobody just...
And this was back in the 30s.
I wonder if the Depression had anything to do with it.
Just, you know, money being taught. Maybe, maybe not.

Yeah. Maybe, I don't know, because things were everywhere else, all the place was open, you know. Open, yeah. Yeah. Just giving dances and stuff, just, the price wasn't high like it is now. You could get a bang for three or four dollars a man a night, you know. Yeah. Two and a half, you know.
Yeah. Well, the high cost of living was lower then. You could do anything you wanted. Anything you wanted.
For sure, you could go get a pound of rice for nickel, a pound of beans for nickel, and get line-yap black pepper and stuff.

Yeah. Well that gross there on the corner of Franklin Speed was right on the corner there. Yeah. All right, he used to sell quartet salt meat, rice, beans, I mean anything you wanted, because he used to give you...
For the five beans and rice on fire for twenty cents.
If you go buy with a nickel, if you buy half stuff, they'd give you a little brass check. Now that represent two cents and a half, if you could go get something with that. Yeah.

Well, Miss Vick on St. Philip and Priya, she used to take a loaf of bread and cut it in half, see, and then cut it that way. Yeah. And you could get a sandwich for a nickel. Yeah. She'd make four nickel sandwiches out of a loaf of bread. Yeah. That's right. Now sandwich costs eighty cents. Or sandwich like that, of course, and dollar man.
That's awful. Yeah. And have a ton of...
